t: You're looking at the statue of Mahatma Gandhi in Parliament Square, by the Scottish sculptor Philip Jackson. Gandhi was an Indian lawyer and anti-colonial nationalist who used nonviolent resistance to lead the campaign for India's independence from British rule. His example went on to inspire movements for civil rights and freedom around the world. The title Mahatma was first applied to him in 1914 in South Africa. Philip Jackson has served as Royal Sculptor, and his work appears in many British cities, as well as in Argentina and Switzerland.
